fresh_leads.title: Software Engineering Intern - 2027 Summer Term
fresh_leads.qualification_text: What we're looking for Actively pursuing a Bachelor/Master in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field Graduating in Fall/Winter 2027 or Spring/Summer 2028. 3.7 GPA Minimum Must have completed an introductory Computer Science course Have advanced programming experience in one or more application or systems languages (Go, Python, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, C/C++, etc.) A problem-solver who thrives in tackling diverse technical challenges and demonstrates a clear track record of growth and learning A take-charge individual who exhibits ownership and takes pride in writing clean, maintainable, and fun code An engineer who can dive deep into open source software, find issues, and fix them. What you'll do As an engineering intern at Atoms, you'll be an integral part of building out the state-of-the-art intelligent machine for the food industry. Your role will encompass a diverse range of responsibilities, including: You will build foundational software systems to enable globally scaled kitchen infrastructure and real estate innovations You test software development methodology in an agile environment You provide ongoing maintenance, support, and enhancements in existing systems and platforms You work alongside other engineers to elevate technology and improve systems overall You write, debug, maintain and test code You design scalable, fault tolerant architectural systems You develop information systems by designing, developing, and installing software solutions You drive innovation within the team and support Atoms' technological advancements Why join us At Atoms, you'll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what's known and building what doesn't yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it's grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow. What else you need to know This role can be based in New York, Seattle, Los Angeles, Mountain View or San Francisco . Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That's why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. The base starting rate for this role is $70.00 per hour. Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications. Program Dates : May - September, our Summer Internship cohort runs from late May through September. Application Timeline: Getting a head start on your job search? So are we! We're building our candidate pipeline now for our upcoming internship positions. Feel free to submit your resume today, we'll be reviewing applications over the coming weeks and will reach out directly if your background is a match when interviews begin in the Fall.

fresh_leads.title: Software Engineering (Engineering Productivity) Intern
fresh_leads.qualification_text: Software Engineering (Engineering Productivity) Intern Burlingame, California Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth. With Pulsar – the world's most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection. OVERVIEW - As a Software Engineer (Engineering Productivity) Intern, you maintain and expand our developer tooling, build system, and internal services to meet developer needs. - You will assist in the development of our internal Bazel tooling, developer tools, CI/CD, and related technologies. - Engineering productivity underlies the entire operation, and can be utilized by every software engineering team in the company to improve their workflows and enable them to write better software, faster. WHAT YOU'LL DO: - Build & CI/CD tooling: Ship improvements to our internal Bazel-based build solution, focused on usability and functionality. - Software integration: Help our assorted tools (IDE, CI/CD, build system, etc) interoperate more closely, creating functionality to bridge gaps between tooling designed and owned by others. PREFERRED ATTRIBUTES: - Excitement for learning. - Interest in improving your own development workflow (think making your own IDE plugins, tools, etc) - Experience tinkering with C++, Rust, Python, and other commonly used languages. - Experience with using git or jj for version control. - Interest in embedded systems and robotics. For U.S. Roles: To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). For U.K. Roles: To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC). For Canada Roles: Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

fresh_leads.title: Systems Intern - Validation, Software, Design, Architecture & Packaging (USA)
fresh_leads.location: Austin, Texas, United States; Santa Clara, California, United States
fresh_leads.qualification_text: you have one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team below and location that fits best. Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs. System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware. System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint. System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals. Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis. This role is on-site, based out of Austin, TX or Santa Clara, CA. Who You Are Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog). Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical. Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs). What We Need Systems & Silicon Validation: Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications. System Software: Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware. System Design & Architecture: Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs. Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design: Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis What You Will Learn Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips. Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal. Mechanical & thermal engineering for electronics by learning how structural stress, heat dissipation, thermal expansion, and mechanical shock affect the structural integrity and performance of PCBs and packages. Cross-functional collaboration working alongside world-class architects, mechanical designers, package engineers, and software teams to understand how complex, large-scale chip ecosystems are built from scratch. USA Hiring Timelines This internship opportunity is available throughout our 3 terms with the following corresponding recruitment cycles: Winter Term: Jan–Apr work term, Sept–Dec recruit.
